gap: No result ChatGPT got states Clubic's measurements of the TerraMaster F6-424 Max over 10GbE in RAID 5 (about 1,150 MB/s sequential read, 797 MB/s write, at most 36.8 dB, over 60 W with six drives), so ChatGPT's repeated 'similar to the DXP6800 Pro' claim for this model rested on spec sheets alone.
standout_why: StarryHope (cited, 2026-11-02) quotes only Notebookcheck's DXP6800 Pro idle draw of 37–42 W with four drives. It covers no TerraMaster or QNAP model and has no transcode, throughput or noise figure for any 6-bay unit. Notebookcheck's DXP6800 Pro review (cited) measured iPerf3 at 9.5 Gbit/s, noise at 34.6–43 dB(A) and power at 22.4 W without drives and 36.6–41.9 W with four. That covers only the UGREEN, and our current page already carries all of it. The NASCompares F6-424 Max review is not in the result sets, and it only lists '35W idle / 70W load' in a spec table with no stated method or drive count. QNAP's pages carry only QNAP's own power figures. None of the result pages has any reviewer measurement of the F6-424 Max, F6-425 Pro, DXP6800 Ultra or TVS-h674, and none has a measured Plex stream count for any candidate.
decides: It confirms rather than changes the pick. A named lab measured the F6-424 Max, the main i5-1235U/dual-10GbE rival to the DXP6800 Pro, at roughly 1.15 GB/s read and 0.8–0.9 GB/s write over 10GbE. That backs the 'same class' claim with data. It does not separate the two boxes: neither has a measured Plex transcode count, so the choice still comes down to price, the PCIe slot and Thunderbolt 4. The DXP6800 Pro stays the pick and the F6-424 Max the value alternative when it sells under $1,000.

unsourced: A measured count of simultaneous Plex 4K or 4K HDR tone-mapped transcodes for any candidate (DXP6800 Pro, DXP6800 Ultra, F6-424 Max, F6-425 Pro, TVS-h674). I checked Notebookcheck, Dong Knows Tech, Clubic, NASCompares, Profesional Review and searches for DXP8800 Plus/i5-1235U tests. None reports a stream count with a stated method. A UK repair-shop blog claims '3 simultaneous 4K transcodes' on the DXP6800 Pro with no method; I did not open it and left it out.

Reviewer-measured power, throughput or noise for the QNAP TVS-h674. Profesional Review (José Antonio Castillo, 2023-01-30, i3-12100 unit) gives no measurements. The only power figures I found are QNAP's own (39.911 W disk standby, 79.363 W typical, full of WD10EFRX drives). No StorageReview, TechRadar or ServeTheHome test of the non-T TVS-h674 turned up.
Measurements for the TerraMaster F6-425 Pro. NASCompares' piece is a hands-on that says noise, thermals and sustained performance were still to be tested.
Measurements for the UGREEN DXP6800 Ultra. Search found only UGREEN's ratings (about 43 W active, 25 W hibernation) and a How-To Geek score quoted second-hand. I did not open the How-To Geek review.
A separate idle-power figure for the F6-424 Max. NASCompares' '35W idle / 70W load' sits in a spec table with no method or drive count.
